# Obadiah Chapter 1 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 339v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/OBA_001_page_001.jpg

---

**1** This is the vision that came to Obadiah. Here is what the Lord GOD says about Edom: We have received a message from the LORD — an envoy has been dispatched to the nations: "Get ready! Let's go to war against her!"

**2** "Look — I am going to make you the smallest of nations. You will be completely despised. **3** Your arrogance has gone to your head — you who live high up in the rock cliffs, making your home in the heights, saying to yourself, 'No one can touch me up here!' **4** Even if you fly as high as an eagle, even if you build your nest among the stars — I will bring you crashing down," declares the LORD.

**5** "If thieves broke into your house — and oh, what a disaster is coming! — wouldn't they steal only what they wanted? If grape pickers came to your vineyard, wouldn't they leave a few grapes behind? **6** But you, Esau — you will be stripped bare! Every hidden treasure will be found and taken!"

**7** "Your own allies will turn on you. Your trusted friends will deceive you and overpower you. Those who ate at your table will set a trap for you — and you won't see it coming."

**8** "On that day," declares the LORD, "I will wipe out the wise men of Edom and every trace of understanding from the hill country of Esau. **9** Your warriors will be terrified, Teman, and every last soldier on Mount Esau will be slaughtered."

**10** "Because of the violence you did to your brother Jacob, you will be covered in shame and wiped out forever. **11** On the day you stood and watched — the day when foreigners marched off with his wealth, when invaders poured through his gates and divided up Jerusalem by casting lots — you were no better than any of them."

**12** "You should not have gloated over your brother's misfortune. You should not have celebrated Judah's destruction. You should not have taunted them in their darkest hour. **13** You should not have marched through my people's gates on their day of disaster. You should not have stood there enjoying their suffering. You should not have helped yourself to their wealth. **14** You should not have waited at the crossroads to cut down those trying to escape. You should not have handed their survivors over to the enemy."

**15** "The day of the LORD is almost here — and it's coming for every nation. What you have done will be done to you. Your own actions will come back on your own head. **16** Just as you drank on my holy mountain, so all the nations will drink — drink and drink until they stagger and disappear, as if they had never existed."

**17** "But on Mount Zion there will be a remnant that escapes, and it will be a holy place. The descendants of Jacob will reclaim what was rightfully theirs. **18** Jacob's descendants will be a fire, Joseph's descendants a flame, and Esau's descendants dry straw. They will burn them up completely — not one of Esau's descendants will survive." The LORD has spoken.

**19** People from the Negev will take over the hill country of Esau. People from the western foothills will occupy Philistine territory. They will take over the lands of Ephraim and Samaria, while Benjamin claims Gilead. **20** The Israelite exiles in Canaan will extend their territory as far as Zarephath, and the exiles from Jerusalem who are in Sepharad will take over the towns of the Negev. **21** Deliverers will go up on Mount Zion to govern the hill country of Esau. And the kingdom will belong to the LORD.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**The Edom grudge:** This tiny book carries centuries of bad blood. Edom and Israel were "brother nations" — Esau and Jacob, twins who fought from the womb (Genesis 25). When Babylon destroyed Jerusalem in 586 BCE, Edom apparently aided the invaders or at least cheered from the sidelines. For the survivors, this was the ultimate betrayal — your own brother helping your enemy. Obadiah is the biblical response to that wound.

**"You should not have" (vv.12-14):** These eight prohibitions are heartbreaking because they describe what already happened. The Hebrew grammar creates a devastating effect — each command forbids an action that Edom has already committed. They function as an accusation disguised as a warning.

**The kingdom belongs to the LORD (v.21):** The tiniest book in the Old Testament ends with the biggest idea — that all earthly kingdoms, all power struggles between brother nations, all geopolitical maneuvering will finally give way to God's own sovereignty.

*— PNEUMA*
